steps.name: QC + main DE: treated vs control
caveats: 5 samples per group gives limited per-gene power; state that in the summary rather than over-interpreting borderline adjusted p values.
If the matrix turns out to be TPM-like (fractional, per-sample sums near 1e6), do not feed it to DESeq2.
sample_03's group membership must be read from metadata.csv, not assumed.
steps.context: Files: /eval-four-models-v2-without-outlier-n5-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 x 11: gene ID column + 10 sample columns, raw Salmon gene-level output) and /eval-four-models-v2-without-outlier-n5-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (10 x 2: one row per sample with condition; expected 5 treated, 5 control). Organism Homo sapiens (taxon 9606), tissue muscle, unpaired single batch — no batch term. Data profile caveat: sample_03 separates from every other sample on PCA and the sample distance heatmap.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between the 5 treated and 5 control human muscle bulk RNA-seq samples in the 12000-gene Salmon count table, and how does the flagged deviating sample (sample_03) sit in that picture?
constraints: Load counts.csv and metadata.csv; verify 12000 genes x 10 samples and that the 10 sample columns join 1:1 to metadata rows by sample ID, not by position. Report the actual condition factor levels and per-group counts.

Expect Salmon table layout: a 'Name' (gene ID) column followed by one count column per sample. If IDs are not gene symbols, map to HGNC symbols/Entrez via org.Hs.eg.db and report the mapping rate; keep unmapped genes in statistics, exclude them only from symbol-based reporting.

Count-type check before modeling: if essentially all entries are non-negative integers, treat as raw counts and run DESeq2 (design ~ condition, reference = control); if any entries are fractional (length-corrected/TPM-like), run edgeR TMM normalization + limma-voom with the same treated-vs-control contrast. Record which branch was taken and the fraction of non-integer entries.
Low-count filter before DE: keep genes with CPM >= 0.25 in at least 6 of 10 samples; report gene count before and after filtering.
In the DESeq2 branch only, apply apeglm log2FC shrinkage to reported log2FCs.

QC: per-sample total counts and detected-gene counts, PCA on log2-normalized counts, and a sample distance heatmap; explicitly characterize sample_03's separation (which PC(s) it drives, its nearest-neighbor distance) and report which condition it belongs to, read from metadata.
Do not exclude any sample from the main analysis; all 10 samples enter the model.
steps.description: Validate the count matrix and metadata join, characterize sample_03's deviation on QC plots, and run the main treated-vs-control DE on all 10 samples with a model chosen from the count type actually observed.
acceptance_criteria: A DE table with gene ID, symbol, baseMean, log2FC (treated vs control, control as reference), p value, and BH-adjusted p value computed on all 10 samples.
A PCA plot, sample distance heatmap, and per-sample QC table in which sample_03's deviation is characterized and its condition is stated.
An explicit record of the count-type check outcome and the statistical model used (DESeq2/apeglm vs TMM/voom).

plan.title: Muscle treated vs control DE + outlier sensitivity
plan.analytical_narrative: Input is a Salmon gene-level count table (12000 genes x 10 human muscle samples, 5 treated vs 5 control, single batch, unpaired) whose profile explicitly flags an ambiguity: the record does not state whether the counts are raw or length-corrected. T1S1 resolves that empirically (integrality check), confirms the flagged deviation of sample_03, and runs the main treated-vs-control DE — DESeq2 + apeglm if raw integer counts, edgeR TMM + limma-voom if length-corrected. T1S2 reruns the identical pipeline with sample_03 removed (4 vs 5) to quantify how much that single deviating sample drives gene-level results, which matters in a 5-vs-5 design. T1S3 maps the DE result to human pathways (human WikiPathways GMT from the reference store) and GO terms (GO.db, offline), annotating top hits for robustness against sample_03 exclusion.
